body.statement:
The frozen model assumptions do not identify the exact-dose causal curve.  In particular, there exist compatible fixed constants, one observed law \(P\in\mathcal M\), and two full-data witnesses \(P^{\mathrm F}_1\) and \(P^{\mathrm F}_2\) satisfying every membership condition in \(\texttt{def:model-class}\), having the same \((W,A,Y)\)-marginal \(P\), but satisfying
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}_1}[Y(a)]=\theta(a)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}_2}[Y(a)]\ne\theta(a)
\]
for every \(a\in J\).  Hence consistency, the sectionwise conditional-exchangeability assumption, strict overlap, smoothness of the observed regression, and continuity of the chosen conditional potential-outcome mean do not imply the claimed equality uniformly over admissible full-data extensions.
body.justification: The corrected lemma is a load-bearing negative certificate: it shows that the proposed causal interpretation is unavailable under the frozen continuous-dose assumptions.
body.gap: Sectionwise exchangeability and continuity of conditional potential-outcome means do not exclude modifications on the random treatment diagonal.
body.consumer: AHA/CMS interpretation must remain at the observed G-computation curve until a valid causal bridge is supplied.
body.proof_tex:
We give an explicit two-witness certificate.  Choose
\[
d=1,\qquad s=7,\qquad \delta=\frac14,\qquad
c_{\theta}=C_{\theta}=c_p=C_p=c_g=C_g=1,
\qquad v_{\kappa}=V_{\kappa}=\frac1{100},\qquad B=2.
\]
Then \(d\) is a positive integer, \(s=7>3(d+1)=6\), and
\(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  The choices give
\[
c_{\theta}\le C_{\theta},\qquad
c_p\le 1\le C_p,\qquad
c_g\le 1\le C_g,\qquad
v_{\kappa}\le V_{\kappa},
\]
as required by the four ordering compatibility assumptions.  Moreover,
\[
\frac{c_{\theta}}2+\sqrt{v_{\kappa}}
=\frac12+\frac1{10}=\frac35<2=B,
\]
which verifies \(\texttt{ass:bounded-witness-compatibility}\).  Every polynomial used below, and each polynomial entering the definition of \(L_0\), has a finite \(C^s\) norm on its compact domain.  Choose the fixed radius \(L\) at least as large as \(L_0\) and the \(C^s\) norms of the four observed-law primitives displayed below.  This verifies \(\texttt{ass:radius-compatibility}\) and will verify all four smoothness conditions.

On a probability space let \(W\), \(A\), and \(R\) be mutually independent, let \(W\) and \(A\) be uniform on \([0,1]\), and let
\[
\Pr(R=1)=\Pr(R=-1)=\frac12.
\]
Define
\[
Y=A+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10},
\]
and let \(P\) be the law of \((W,A,Y)\).  Since
\[
0\le Y\le \frac65<B,
\]
the law \(P\) satisfies \(\texttt{ass:outcome-bound}\).  Independence and the uniform laws give the everywhere-defined density versions
\[
p(w)=1,\qquad g(a\mid w)=1,\qquad f(a)=\int_0^1g(a\mid w)p(w)\,dw=1.
\]
Consequently
\[
\int_0^1p(w)\,dw=1,
\qquad
\int_0^1g(a\mid w)\,da=1
\quad\text{for every }w\in[0,1],
\]
so \(\texttt{ass:p-normalization}\) and \(\texttt{ass:g-normalization}\) hold.  The equalities \(p=g=1\), together with the chosen constants, also give
\[
c_p\le p(w)\le C_p,
\qquad
c_g\le g(a\mid w)\le C_g,
\]
on their full domains, proving \(\texttt{ass:p-bounds}\) and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\).

Direct conditioning, using \(\mathbb E[R]=0\) and \(R^2=1\), gives the everywhere-defined versions
\[
m(a,w)=a+\frac1{10},
\qquad
r(a,w)=\left(a+\frac1{10}\right)^2+\frac1{100}.
\]
The functions \(p\), \(g\), \(m\), and \(r\) are polynomials and belong to their respective radius-\(L\) Hölder balls by the choice of \(L\).  Thus \(\texttt{ass:p-smooth}\), \(\texttt{ass:g-smooth}\), \(\texttt{ass:m-smooth}\), and \(\texttt{ass:r-smooth}\) hold.  By the definition of the observed G-computation curve and the normalization of \(p\),
\[
\theta(a)=\int_0^1m(a,w)p(w)\,dw
=a+\frac1{10}
\quad\text{for every }a\in[0,1].
\]
It follows that \(\theta\) is nondecreasing, proving \(\texttt{ass:monotone}\), and that
\[
\theta'(a)=1,
\qquad
c_{\theta}\le\theta'(a)\le C_{\theta}
\quad\text{for every }a\in J=[1/4,3/4],
\]
proving \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\).

The definitions of \(\sigma^2\) and \(e\) yield
\[
\sigma^2(a,w)=r(a,w)-m(a,w)^2=\frac1{100},
\qquad
e(a,w)=\frac{g(a\mid w)}{f(a)}=1.
\]
In particular, the division defining \(e\) is legitimate because \(f(a)=1>0\).  From the definitions of \(\xi\) and \(\varepsilon\),
\[
\varepsilon(O)=\frac{Y-m(A,W)}{e(A,W)}=\frac1{10}R.
\]
Therefore the constant version of the conditional second moment is
\[
\kappa(a)=\mathbb E_P\!\left[\varepsilon(O)^2\mid A=a\right]
=\frac1{100}
=v_{\kappa}=V_{\kappa}
\quad\text{for every }a\in J,
\]
which proves \(\texttt{ass:variance}\).

It remains to construct two full-data extensions of this same observed law.  For every \(a\in[0,1]\), define
\[
Y_1(a)=a+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10},
\qquad
Y_2(a)=a+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10}\mathbf 1\{a=A\}.
\]
The map \((a,A,R)\mapsto Y_1(a)\) is Borel measurable.  The same is true for \(Y_2\), because the diagonal \(\{(a,A):a=A\}\) is closed and hence Borel.  Thus each sample path is Borel measurable, and all coordinate evaluations are measurable, so each \(Y_j(\cdot)\) is a random element of the evaluation-sigma-field space \(\mathcal Y_B\).  Furthermore,
\[
-\frac1{10}\le Y_j(a)\le\frac65<B
\quad\text{for every }a\in[0,1]
\quad\text{and }j\in\{1,2\},
\]
so both potential-outcome processes take values in the required range \([-B,B]\).

For \(j\in\{1,2\}\), let \(P_j^{\mathrm F}\) be the law of
\[
\bigl(W,A,Y,\{Y_j(a):a\in[0,1]\}\bigr).
\]
By construction, the \((W,A,Y)\)-marginal of each \(P_j^{\mathrm F}\) is \(P\), proving \(\texttt{ass:observed-marginal}\).  At the realized dose,
\[
Y_1(A)=A+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10}=Y
\]
and
\[
Y_2(A)=A+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10}\mathbf 1\{A=A\}=Y.
\]
Hence both extensions satisfy \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\).

Fix any deterministic \(a\in[0,1]\).  Since \(A\) has a Lebesgue density,
\[
\Pr(A=a)=0.
\]
It follows that
\[
Y_1(a)=a+\frac1{10}R+\frac1{10}
\quad\text{almost surely},
\qquad
Y_2(a)=a+\frac1{10}R
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Each right-hand side is a measurable function of \(R\), whereas \(R\) is independent of \((A,W)\).  Thus, for every pair of bounded Borel functions \(h\) and \(q\),
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[h\{Y_j(a)\}q(A)\mid W\right]
=\mathbb E\!\left[h\{Y_j(a)\}\mid W\right]
 \mathbb E\!\left[q(A)\mid W\right]
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
This conditional factorization proves \(Y_j(a)\perp A\mid W\) for every deterministic \(a\), so both extensions satisfy \(\texttt{ass:exchangeability}\).

Because \(\mathbb E[R]=0\), define
\[
\mu^{\mathrm F}_1(a,w)=a+\frac1{10},
\qquad
\mu^{\mathrm F}_2(a,w)=a.
\]
These functions are jointly Borel measurable and, for every \(w\), are continuous in \(a\).  For each fixed \(a\), the preceding almost-sure formulas and independence of \(R\) and \(W\) show that
\[
\mu^{\mathrm F}_j(a,W)
=\mathbb E_{P_j^{\mathrm F}}[Y_j(a)\mid W]
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
They are therefore versions satisfying every clause of \(\texttt{ass:potential-mean-continuity}\).

All remaining conditions in \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) are observed-law conditions already verified above.  Hence \(P\in\mathcal M\), and both \(P_1^{\mathrm F}\) and \(P_2^{\mathrm F}\) are admissible full-data witnesses for this same member \(P\).  Finally, for every \(a\in J\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_1^{\mathrm F}}[Y_1(a)]
=a+\frac1{10}=\theta(a),
\]
whereas
\[
\mathbb E_{P_2^{\mathrm F}}[Y_2(a)]
=a\ne a+\frac1{10}=\theta(a).
\]
The modification defining \(Y_2\) lies on the random diagonal \(a=A\).  It is null in every deterministic-dose section, so it does not alter sectionwise exchangeability or the continuous conditional-mean versions, while consistency evaluates the process precisely on that diagonal.  This proves the stated failure of exact-dose causal identification under the frozen model.
